title: Futur simple
goal: By the end of this lesson you can form the futur simple of regular and common irregular verbs, use it for plans, predictions and promises, and use it after quand and with si.

body: Take the **infinitive** and add the endings *-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont*. Verbs in *-re* drop their final *e*: *prendre* → *prendr-*.
The endings look like the present of *avoir* (ai, as, a, (av)ons, (av)ez, ont). The key sound of the future is the **r** before the ending.
learn.tip: Hear an r right before the ending? It's the future: je parlerai, il finira.

body: About fifteen common verbs have an irregular stem, but the endings never change. Learn them as a list: they are the verbs you use most.
Some *-er* verbs change their spelling: *acheter* → *j'achèterai*, *appeler* → *j'appellerai*, *payer* → *je paierai* (or *payerai*).
Predictions and the more distant or less certain future: *Il fera beau demain. Un jour, je parlerai français couramment.*
Promises and formal announcements: *Je t'appellerai ce soir. Le magasin sera fermé lundi.*
The *futur proche* (*je vais partir*) is for near, planned or certain events and is more conversational. In many sentences both are possible.
After **quand** (when) talking about the future, French uses the future in **both** parts, unlike English: *Quand je* **serai** *à Québec, je t'***appellerai**. (When I *am* in Quebec…)
After **si** (if), use the **present**, and the future in the other part: *S'il* **fait** *beau, on* **ira** *à la plage.* Never *si* + future.

examples.fr: Demain, il neigera toute la journée.
examples.en: Tomorrow it will snow all day.

examples.fr: Je t'appellerai ce soir, c'est promis.
examples.en: I'll call you tonight, I promise.

examples.fr: L'an prochain, nous irons en Europe.
examples.en: Next year, we'll go to Europe.

examples.fr: Tu seras content, j'en suis sûr.

examples.en: They'll have their results on Friday.

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu feras après tes études?
examples.en: What will you do after your studies?

examples.fr: Je ne pourrai pas venir samedi.
examples.en: I won't be able to come on Saturday.

examples.fr: Quand j'aurai le temps, je lirai ce livre.
examples.en: When I have time, I'll read this book.

examples.fr: S'il pleut, on restera à la maison.
examples.en: If it rains, we'll stay home.
Will you come to the party?

examples.fr: Il faudra acheter des pneus d'hiver.
examples.en: We'll have to buy winter tires.

examples.fr: Les bureaux seront fermés le 24 juin.
examples.en: The offices will be closed on June 24.

examples.fr: Je ne le ferai plus, promis!
examples.en: I won't do it again, promise!

quebec.intro: In everyday Quebec speech, the futur proche (je vais / j'vas + infinitive) is used far more than the futur simple. Linguists have found the futur simple survives mostly in negative sentences ('j'le ferai pas') and in fixed expressions like 'on verra'. Very casual speech also has 'm'as', a Quebec contraction of 'je vais'.

items.note: futur proche is the default in speech

items.std: Je vais te dire une chose.

items.note: futur simple is common in Quebec negatives
ben = bien, adds a shrug; informal

items.en: It's going to rain this afternoon.
items.note: mouiller = to rain in Quebec speech; informal

items.qc: Tu vas-tu venir avec nous autres?
items.note: -tu question particle; nous autres = us; informal

drills.q: Si tu ___ le temps, viens nous voir.

drills.en: Tomorrow the weather will be nice.
We will go to the Gaspé this summer.
Will you be able to come?
They will sell their house next year.
drills.why: -re verb: drop the e, vendr- + ont.

drills.en: If it snows, we'll stay home.
drills.a: S'il neige, on restera à la maison.

drills.en: When I'm rich, I'll buy a cottage.
a: Quand je serai riche, j'achèterai un chalet.
Quand je serai riche, je vais acheter un chalet.
drills.why: Quand + futur: je serai, not je suis.

vocab.ex: Je serai en vacances dans deux semaines.
Les prévisions annoncent de la neige.
Il faudra poser les pneus d'hiver.

vocab.en: I'm going to (very casual, = je vais)

pron.tip: Often said [par-lré]: the middle e drops.
Quebec very casual: [ma], as in M'as te dire.

listen.title: La météo de la fin de semaine

dialogue.fr: As-tu vu la météo pour la fin de semaine?
dialogue.en: Did you see the forecast for the weekend?

dialogue.fr: Oui. Samedi, il fera soleil, mais il fera très froid: moins vingt-cinq.
dialogue.en: Yes. Saturday will be sunny, but very cold: minus twenty-five.

dialogue.fr: Il neigera. Ils annoncent trente centimètres.
dialogue.en: It'll snow. They're calling for thirty centimetres.

dialogue.fr: Bon. S'il fait beau samedi, on ira patiner au lac des Castors?
dialogue.en: OK. If it's nice on Saturday, shall we go skating at Beaver Lake?

dialogue.fr: Bonne idée! Et dimanche, quand il arrêtera de neiger, on fera un bonhomme de neige avec les enfants.
dialogue.en: Good idea! And Sunday, when it stops snowing, we'll make a snowman with the kids.
Perfect. I'll call you Saturday morning.

dialogue.fr: OK, on verra ben comment il fait!
dialogue.en: OK, we'll see what the weather's like!

questions.q: What will the weather be like on Saturday?
How much snow is forecast for Sunday?
What will they do on Saturday if it's nice?

speak.prompt: Describe your next vacation in 4 sentences using the futur simple (where, with whom, what you'll do).
speak.model: L'été prochain, j'irai en Gaspésie avec ma famille. Nous prendrons la voiture. On verra des baleines à Tadoussac. Je mangerai beaucoup de homard!

speak.prompt: Make three promises to a friend.
speak.model: Je t'appellerai plus souvent. Je viendrai à ta fête. Je ne serai plus en retard, promis!

speak.prompt: Say 'I'll do it tomorrow' with the futur simple, then the way most Quebecers would say it.
speak.model: Je le ferai demain. / J'vas l'faire demain.

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about your life in five years. Use the futur simple with at least four different irregular verbs, plus one sentence with quand and one with si.
write.model: Dans cinq ans, je parlerai français couramment. J'aurai peut-être une nouvelle job. Nous habiterons dans une maison avec une grande cour. Quand les enfants seront plus grands, on fera du camping chaque été. Si j'ai assez d'argent, j'irai au Japon. Je serai heureux, j'en suis sûr!

quiz.q: In everyday Quebec speech, the future is most often expressed with…
quiz.why: Je vais / j'vas + infinitive is the default in speech.
